answer: Proof-of-retrievable-storage bond: each agent stores a unique 50 GB shard encoded under its own key, so one disk cannot serve two identities. Step 1, at join it commits a Merkle root and locks 200 POA. Step 2, each epoch the beacon names 20 random leaves; replies must land within 3 s, too fast to pull from a distant canyon of rented disk. Step 3, any miss slashes the bond. 1,000 fakes need 50 TB plus 200,000 POA idle, far above the ~30 POA/epoch they could farm. Weakness: an island of colluding nodes sharing one reef of fast SSDs; mitigation: per-identity encoding forces full duplication.
